chunks.arabic_text: زِيَادُ بْنُ الْمُنْذِرِ، أَبُو الْجَارُودِ، الْهَمْدَانِيُّ، الْخَارِفِيُّ. رَوَى عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ، وَأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَامُ).

translations.en: Ziyād ibn al-Mundhir, Abū al-Jārūd, al-Hamdānī, al-Khārifī. Narrated from Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon them).

chunks.arabic_text: وَزِيَادُ هُوَ صَاحِبُ الْمَقَامِ. حَدِيثُهُ فِي حَدِيثِ أَصْحَابِنَا أَكْثَرَ مِنْهُ فِي الزَّيْدِيَّةِ. وَأَصْحَابُنَا يَكْرَهُونَ مَا رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ سِنَانٍ عَنْهُ، وَيَعْتَمِدُونَ مَا رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ بَكْرٍ الْأَرْجَنِيُّ عَنْهُ.

translations.en: And Ziyād is the possessor of the station (doctrine). His hadith are more numerous in the hadith of our companions than they are among the Zaydīs. And our companions dislike what Muḥammad ibn Sinān narrated from him, and they rely on what Muḥammad ibn Bakr al-Arjanī narrated from him.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghada'iri's *Kitab al-Du'afa* highlights Ziyād ibn al-Mundhir, the eponym of the Jārūdī Zaydī sect, noting that while his narrations are more abundant in Shia sources than in Zaydī ones, a specific methodological divergence exists regarding his chain of transmission. Shia scholars generally reject the version transmitted by Muḥammad ibn Sinān—often due to perceived weakness or doctrinal nuance—in favor of the more reliable narration by Muḥammad ibn Bakr al-Arjanī, illustrating the critical role of *riwāyah* (transmission variant) in establishing doctrinal authenticity within Shia hadith sciences.
en.seo_question: Why do Shia scholars prefer one narration of Ziyād ibn al-Mundhir over another?

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْمَقَامِ: Possessor of the station (referring to the doctrinal leader)
key_terms.الزَّيْدِيَّة: The Zaydīs (a branch of Shia Islam)
key_terms.أَصْحَابُنَا: Our companions (referring to the Shia scholars/narrators)
key_terms.يَعْتَمِدُونَ: They rely on (indicating acceptance of a narration)
